messages:
ana: Heads-up—noticed a small but steady memory growth on one of the long-context perf jobs. It looks correlated with KV cache hit rate drops after ~60k tokens.
chris: Can you paste the log snippet? which job?
ana: repro is the `retry-qa-long-context` harness on ded1; below is the eviction log around the spike:
ana: ```
[2026-06-12T14:02:13Z] kvcache: page_alloc id=42 size=4096 slots=128
[2026-06-12T14:02:13Z] kvcache: append tag=0x7f offset=24576 len=512 req_id=abcd1234
[2026-06-12T14:02:14Z] kvcache: evict page=41 tombstone=1 last_req=abcd1220
[2026-06-12T14:02:15Z] kvcache: append tag=0x7f offset=24576 len=512 req_id=abcd1250
[2026-06-12T14:02:15Z] kvcache: warning: slot 192 reused without clear (align mismatch)
```
liam: that `slot 192 reused` message is new—did we add extra assertions? I only remember `reuse-check` for session tags.
ana: I added a quick assertion in the debug build to print misaligns. It triggers when an append's token index doesn't match the page offset * token_size.
perf-jen: could be a windowing bug: when we compact fragments we recompute offsets using the oldest-seen base token, but batched requests may have different base tokens and cause an off-by-one in tag alignment.
chris: Repro steps? I can try locally.
ana: Run the harness with `CONTEXT_LEN=120000 BATCH_SIZE=8` and `KV_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=4096`. After ~30 mins you should see the misaligned append warning and memory creeping up in `smem` by ~30-40MB.
devops-bot: deploy-trigger: started job build/runtime-debug:2026-06-12-0210 (track: debug).
liam: I instrumented `kv_dump` to print fragment headers. Here's one corrupted header sequence we saw: `frag[id=7]: base_tok=100000, length=512, page_off=24576` then later `frag[id=7]: base_tok=100050, length=512, page_off=24576` — base_tok changed without page movement.
chris: That smells like concurrent reuse: a page freed and reallocated, but the fragment index table wasn't zeroed and we applied a different base_tok to the old page.
ana: Reproduced with `--enable-concurrent-merge`. If I disable concurrent merges, leak stops.
perf-jen: Is it safe to just serialize merges? that could hurt throughput. Maybe we can zero the header on free and add a fence/op ordering to make header writes atomic.
liam: Proposed fix: on free, write a tombstone tag (0x0) and do a full memory barrier before allowing reallocation. Also, when allocating, validate that fragment base_tok matches expected and otherwise deny reuse (force fresh page).
chris: Quick patch idea: in page_alloc path, memset header to 0xff and set a generation counter incremented on free. On append, check generation matches the index table's view. Adds 8 bytes per page.
ana: I ran the generation-counter patch: no warnings after same-run length (1h). Memory flat. Throughput down only ~1.2% in microbench.
perf-jen: Good tradeoff. Can you add a small perf test and a unit that fuzzes concurrent free/append? We should catch this in CI.
liam: I'll add a stress test that spins up N appenders and M mergers for 5 minutes with randomized token bases.
chris: Also add an observability metric: `kvcache.reuse.misaligned` counter and an alert if >0 for 5m on prod flag.
devops-bot: deploy-status: runtime-debug:2026-06-12-0210 succeeded on ded1.
ana: I'll open a PR with the generation-counter + zeroing + metric. Tagging @perf-jen for the perf test.
perf-jen: thanks — include the smem and perf-run logs. We'll run a 24h soak on the ded pool before backporting to stable. :thumbsup:
chris: Nice catch. This explains a few flaky long-request regressions we've seen in the wild.
liam: filing a follow-up to audit other alloc paths (prefetch, page-merge) for similar races.
ana: thanks all, closing the loop once PR merges.
